newsitem.title: INDIA: Gold-Indian sub-continent prices seen subdued.
newsitem.headline: Gold-Indian sub-continent prices seen subdued.

text.p: A temporary lull in India's marriage season demand is expected to push gold prices down in the current week while a subdued world trend may pressure them further, dealers said on Monday.
"There's a temporary slump in demand. But I expect prices to move upwards within a week," said Bombay Bullion Association president Makhan Lal Damani.
Dealers said imports of gold and silver under special import licences (SILs) had been higher than before. Special import licences are issued against export earnings of traders and are traded openly.

"The premium for acquiring these SILs has fallen to around 10.65 percent from 14 percent in the last few days because of their easy availablity following a recent liberal export-import policy," said bullion dealer Bhayabhai Sanghavi.
He said many Indian expatriates and local traders had booked gold imports, taking advantage of a recent slide in international prices.

Earlier this month, India's political uncertainty kept gold prices firm. Inder Kumar Gujral, India's new prime minister, assumed office at the head of a coalition government last week. He replaced Prime Minister Deve Gowda in the 13-party coalition government after its defeat on April 11.
In the week to Monday, gold prices fell 50 rupees to 4,780 rupees per 10 grammes on the Bombay bullion market.
Dealers in Karachi, the main commercial city of the neighbouring Pakistan, said they expected prices to remain subdued amid low demand this week.
Gold was being traded in a narrow range as jewellers reported low sales, one dealer said.
In Dubai, gold traders said business in the week to Sunday was buoyant, thanks to frantic retail jewellery sales at the end of a month-long shopping promotion.
But the price of investment bars and coins in the local market stayed under pressure, trading in narrow ranges in line with international bullion, they said.
The festival in Dubai, the market feeding demand in India and Pakistan, generated additional business in gold, estimated between seven and 10 tonnes in the current month.
While traders said local retail sales would no doubt fall with the end of the shopping promotion, they forecast a further pick up in demand from India as the country's second wedding
season gets into full swing.
